interactables.name: Basil
interactables.text:
The Gardener, [Basil], is trimming a hedge that has nothing left to give.
'Oh good,' he tells it, not looking up.
'A cat. Cats are natural. Cats belong outside. Like ALL animals.' Snip. Snip.

topics.prompt: Watch his hands while he trims
topics.text:
The shears wobble mid-snip.
'Animals belong in [Nature],' he announces - to the hedge, to the fountain, to the concept of justice.
'[A cage is a prison] with better catering.' He glances at the mansion.
'Not that I would DO anything about it. That would be wrong. Probably.'

'The mud? BULBS. I was planting bulbs.' He holds up a [mud-caked glove] as evidence, realizes evidence is exactly the problem, and puts it behind his back.
'Daffodils. For spring. Ask the flower bed.' The flower bed, [freshly turned], backs him up. His other hand, you notice, is bare.

topics.prompt: Stare from his bare left hand to the mansion. Slowly.
topics.text: The snipping stops. The fountain burbles. Somewhere, a gull. His bare hand curls closed. You wait the way only a cat can wait.|'ALRIGHT. FINE. It is my glove. By the cage. [I broke the latch] - me, with the shears, just before six. Then the front door went, and I panicked, and I ran for the garden.' It falls out of him like loose soil.|'I hid behind the shed. Rudebeak let HIMSELF out - went straight to his bird bath, happy as spring. Then one of those television people came wheeling [big black boxes] through, and I stayed hidden. I am a coward, cat. But I am not a thief.'

interactables.text: Heavy iron [Pruning Shears] left near the fountain. The blade tips are [slightly bent] - the kind of bend you'd get forcing a metal latch.

Behind the potting shed, under a tarp thrown in a hurry: two big black road cases stenciled 'STUDIO 4 - THIS SIDE UP - FRAGILE.' Heavy latches, thick [foam-lined] walls. You press an ear to one. [Silence]. The deep, upholstered kind. The grass around them is pressed flat by [heavy boot prints].
A stone bird bath near the hedgerow. A few [bright feathers] float on the surface - Rudebeak's distinctive markings. Still crisp, not waterlogged. He was here [this evening].

localDeductionSentence: [Basil] swears he spent the whole evening out here, and the [freshly planted bed] backs him up. But his [bent shears] would fit a wrenched cage latch, and the [crisp feathers] in the bird bath say Rudebeak made it to the garden alive. The potting shed has the best view of it all - and someone stood behind it, holding something heavy.
